rows.text: Yuriko's trigger fires for EVERY Ninja that connects, and the damage is the mana value of the card you reveal. So the deck is built around a contradiction that only makes sense here: it runs some of the most expensive cards in Magic precisely because it never intends to cast them. Draco reveals for sixteen. Dig Through Time reveals for eight and still costs two to cast. Every Ninja that gets through is a card AND a chunk of everyone's life total.

rows.name: Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow
rows.text: commander ninjutsu, so she comes back from the command zone for {U}{B} every time. Every Ninja connection reveals your top card, puts it in your HAND, and drains each opponent for its mana value.
Note the changelings count. Changeling Outcast and Mothdust Changeling are every creature type, so they are Ninjas — they are both the enabler AND a trigger.
Ninjutsu goes on the stack AFTER blockers are declared. Attack with the one-drop, wait for no blocks, then swap. The Ninja arrives already unblocked.

rows.name: Draco
rows.text: mana value SIXTEEN. Sixteen life from each opponent on a single flip. Its domain discount makes it castable in a pinch, but you are never casting it.

rows.name: Dig Through Time
rows.text: printed mana value eight, and delve usually makes it cost two. The best card in the deck — cheap to cast, enormous to reveal.

rows.name: Murderous Cut
rows.text: mana value five, delve makes it one. Removal that doubles as a flip.
Everything above roughly three mana value is a real hit in a four-player pod. The deck's curve looks clumsy on paper and is deliberate.
These exist to attack on turn one or two and then get swapped away.

rows.name: Changeling Outcast
rows.text: one mana, cannot block, cannot BE blocked, and it is a Ninja in its own right.

rows.name: Gudul Lurker
rows.text: unblockable, and megamorph gives it a second life later.

rows.text: a flying Faerie every upkeep, forever. Endless enablers.

rows.text: a deathtouch Snake every upkeep — a blocker when you need one and a body to swap when you do not.

rows.name: Ingenious Infiltrator
rows.text: a card for EVERY Ninja that connects, not just itself. With three attackers that is three cards on top of three Yuriko triggers.

rows.name: Fallen Shinobi

rows.text: tutors the next Ninja every connection, and makes any Ninja unblockable for {2}.

rows.name: Dokuchi Silencer

rows.name: Mistblade Shinobi

rows.name: Moon-Circuit Hacker

rows.name: Azra Smokeshaper
rows.text: cheap ninjutsu, and it makes a creature indestructible on arrival — which saves the attack from a blocker or a sweeper.
Yuriko puts the revealed card in your hand, so a good top card is a card AND damage. These let you choose it.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a one-mana unblockable creature. Changeling Outcast, Ornithopter or Gudul Lurker on turn one means Yuriko is on the battlefield on turn two, and that is four or five extra triggers over the game.
Check the top before you swing when you can. A Brainstorm or Ponder in your first main phase turns a random flip into a sixteen-damage Draco.

rows.name: Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow
rows.text: ninjutsu her from the COMMAND ZONE. She does not need to be in your hand, and the commander tax applies to casting, not to ninjutsu — so she comes back for {U}{B} every single time they kill her.
Attack with everything cheap, every turn. The trigger is per Ninja, so three small connections beat one big one, and Reconnaissance-style caution costs you more than the chip damage saves.
